turns.text: ok so i got handed the cost model piece for case comp at midnight basically. team of four, its nov 8 at bayshore. what do judges actually look for in these

Congrats on getting a defined piece. Judging varies by event, but regional supply-chain case competitions usually score on:

1. **Analytical rigor**: are the numbers right, and are assumptions explicit and defensible?
2. **Recommendation quality**: a clear, actionable answer, not just analysis.
3. **Feasibility**: can the company implement it (timeline, risk, capacity)?
4. **Financial impact**: cost savings or ROI, with payback period.
5. **Presentation and Q&A**: clarity, teamwork, handling tough questions.
6. **Creativity**: a differentiated idea grounded in the data.

For the cost model specifically, judges tend to reward transparency: assumptions listed up front and a sensitivity analysis. Want me to lay out what the model should include?
yes pls, tight table. its almost midnight lol

| Component | What to include | Why judges care |
|---|---|---|
| Transportation | Cost per mile or per shipment, mode mix, fuel surcharges, empty-mile share | Usually the largest lever |
| Warehousing | Labor, rent or cost per pallet position, utilities, handling cost per unit | Shows facility trade-offs |
| Inventory carrying | Capital cost, storage, shrinkage, obsolescence (often 15-25% of inventory value per year) | Links service level to cost |
| Order/admin | Processing, systems, customer service | Often overlooked |
| Fixed vs variable | Separate them explicitly | Needed for scenarios |
| One-time costs | Implementation, equipment, training | Feeds payback and ROI |
| Service impact | Lead time, fill rate, penalties for stockouts | Cost cuts that hurt service lose points |
| Baseline vs proposed | Side-by-side totals, savings, payback, NPV | The headline number |
| Sensitivity | Best, base, worst case on fuel, volume, labor | Shows risk awareness |
| Assumptions log | Every input with source | Makes the model defensible |

Tip: put the assumptions on one slide or appendix page so Q&A goes smoothly. If you share the case data, I can help structure the spreadsheet.
thx. also should the model be one tab or split by cost type

Split it:

- **Inputs/Assumptions**: all editable numbers in one place
- **Baseline**: current-state costs
- **Proposed**: new scenario, same structure
- **Summary**: savings, payback, charts
- **Sensitivity**: scenario toggles

Everything links back to Inputs, so a change updates the whole workbook. Color-code input cells (blue) and formulas (black). Then teammates can audit it quickly.
